newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds rose to record highs on Tuesday, supported by positive EMU comments and gains in German Bunds and U.S. Treasuries.
The 10-year future rose 149 basis points from yesterday to 108.75, after it broke a string of resistances. The previous record high was 108.42, hit on October 9.

"The big news today was again a big U.S. hedge fund buying Spanish and Italian bonds. We are almost at the end of the year and it makes very likely they have decided to stay without selling at least until 1997," a dealer in Madrid said.
A good result in the 10-year auction also gave bonos support.
A bond-friendly tone was provided by international markets. Good news on Yeltsin's health after his surgery supported Bunds, while forecasts for today's U.S election pushed Treasuries up.

But peripheral European markets did even better. The 10-year bono-Bund spread declined to 166 basis points from 178 this morning, while the differential over Italian Btps remained unchanged at around 30 basis points.
Tomorrow's Treasury auction of five and 15-year bonds should see a sharp decline in yields, especially in the longer maturity, dealers said.
